title: Mini mentor-led SDK drop-in lab syllabus
body:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, repeatable syllabus for 45–60 minute mentor-led drop-in SDK labs. Target audience: new integrators (engineers) who have signed up for Redwood and completed the self-serve quickstart, but want hands-on pairing to get the first end-to-end flow working and instrumented.

Why this format?
- Short, high-signal sessions reduce friction for busy engineers.
- Mentor pairing accelerates debugging and teaches our troubleshooting heuristics.
- Focused micro-tasks enable measurable outcomes (PR, telemetry, smoke demo).

Prereqs (for attendee)
- Redwood account + API key (or sandbox token)
- Laptop with Node 18+ or Python 3.10+
- GitHub account and willingness to open a small PR to example repos
- Basic terminal comfort

Mentor checklist (1 per session)
- Join Slack channel #sdk-dropins 5 minutes early and ping "mentor:available"
- Open the curated sandbox repo (github link above) and ensure the sample app builds locally
- Confirm recording policy / permission with attendee (if recording)
- Keep a template PR ready: small change that exercises generation, telemetry, and error path

Session plan (60 minutes)
- 00:00–05:00 Quick intros + desired outcome (attendee says success = ?)
- 05:00–12:00 Live demo: mentor runs through the minimal app (show request/response, streaming if relevant)
- 12:00–40:00 Paired work: attendee implements a single feature and opens a draft PR
  - Mentor plays coach, not driver; use "driver–navigator" pattern
  - Swap roles if helpful (mentor types for 3–4 minutes to unblock)
- 40:00–50:00 Telemetry & smoke: add a single metric (latency histogram or request count) and run a smoke test
- 50:00–55:00 Failure injection: simulate network timeout or 429 and demonstrate fallback policy
- 55:00–60:00 Debrief + next steps (file PR, link testing checklist, schedule follow-up if needed)

Micro-tasks (pick 1 per session)
- Task A: First commit — wire the SDK client, call /v1/generate, render output in demo page
- Task B: Instrument telemetry — emit a metric and a trace span for request latency to our example observability bridge
- Task C: Add fallback route — configure a lower-cost model variant and exercise automatic fallback in congested mode
- Task D: Streaming UI — convert blocking generation to streaming and show progressive render
- Task E: Edge-case recovery — implement retry/backoff for 5xx vs no-retry for 4xx and verify behavior with a mock server

Sample mentor prompts (to scaffold conversation)
- "What would make this session valuable for you in 30 minutes?"
- "Let's aim to ship a small PR with a test — could you open the PR when you hit your first success?"
- "If we hit a rate limit, what's your preferred behavior: fail fast, degrade gracefully, or queue?"

Failing fast vs graceful degradation (teaching point)
- Explain tradeoffs using real app examples:
  - Chat UI: prefer streaming + graceful degrade (partial answers)
  - Batch job: prefer fail-fast and retry logic
- Show sample config snippets from our example repo for both behaviors

Troubleshooting rubric (mentor reference)
- Step 1: reproduce locally with minimal input (isolate variables)
- Step 2: check SDK and runtime logs (token-level latency if available)
- Step 3: toggle debug flags in client to get verbose wire logs
- Step 4: if model output quality is surprising, run the same prompt against a known-good model variant and compare tokens

Telem quick recipe (5–10 minutes)
- Add a counter: redwood.request.count = 1 per call
- Add histogram: redwood.request.latency_ms
- Emit errors with tag redwood.error.type = {timeout, rate_limit, server}
- Wire to the example observability bridge (sample env var: OBS_BRIDGE_URL)

Example commands (node)
- npm install @redwood/inference
- export REDWOOD_API_KEY=xxxx
- node examples/basic-generate.js

Example minimal PR description template (mentor provides)
- Title: "feat(example): add basic sdk generate + telemetry"
- Body: short description, how to run locally, screenshot/gif of demo, checklist: 
  - [ ] call succeeds locally
  - [ ] telemetry emitted to test bridge
  - [ ] adds test that mocks 429 path

Classroom logistics + scale
- Best cadence: 3–5 drop-ins per week (60 minutes) with rotating mentors
- Keep sessions lightweight so mentors can do 6–8 per week
- Capture short notes after each session into a central spreadsheet (date, attendee, outcome, blockers)

Post-session artifacts (mentor responsibility)
- Link draft PR into the session row in the spreadsheet
- Add short notes in Slack thread: what was taught and any followups
- If the attendee found a product bug or missing doc, open a ticket (LINEAR-xxxx) and tag eng-docs

Open TODOs (this doc)
- [ ] Add a one-page printable cheat sheet for mentors (debug commands, common errors)
- [ ] Create a pinned Slack thread with exemplar PRs from past sessions
- [ ] Add a short video demo (3–4 minutes) showing the whole flow (demo => PR => telemetry)

Notes to self (informal)
- Pairing is most effective when mentors avoid taking over for long stretches; keep explanations short and iterative.
- Prefer to end with a concrete artifact (PR, ticket) rather than a vague "I understand"
- Consider offering a follow-up 20-minute sync within 48 hours to review PR feedback

Relevant links and artifacts
- Sandbox repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-examples
- Onboarding checklist (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEVX/SDK+Onboarding
- Recording/playbook for mentors: LINK_TO_WIKI_PLACEHOLDER

If you run a session using this syllabus, drop a quick note in #sdk-dropins with date+attendee so we can track adoption and refine the curriculum.

-- Sofia
